subject: Re: KineticPay discovery — token economics & pilot affordability
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Arielle Kwon <arielle.k@kineticpay.com>, Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@kineticpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-27T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: KineticPay discovery — token economics & pilot affordability

Arielle / Tom — thanks again for your time today. Below is a concise recap from our call and suggested next steps so procurement and engineering have a clear short list. Please flag anything I missed.

Quick recap of pain & goals
- Primary pain: inference cost sensitivity on high-volume reconciliation flow (average prompt length ~220 tokens, spike at month-end).
- SLA need: consistent 500 qps peak for reconciliation windows; acceptable P95 latency <= 350ms for customer-facing notes.
- Goal: deliver 60–70% effective per-inference cost reduction for the reconciliation pipeline within pilot constraints (not necessarily model-level parity yet).

Key cost levers we discussed (high level)
- Batching: grouping user requests where latency allowance exists (non-real-time backfill) — expected token throughput improvements of 1.6–2.3x in these paths.
- Prefix/KV caching: reuse previously-computed context for repeated merchant/ledger lookups — 10–25% token hit-rate expected based on your traffic pattern sample.
- Quantization & model-family routing: fall back to smaller quantized variants for low-risk confirmations to reduce per-token compute cost by 30–40%.

Preliminary TCO framing (back-of-envelope)
- Naive hosted usage today: ~1.2M tokens/day for reconciliation; estimated baseline monthly spend ~$18k/month on current provider.
- Pilot target (2–4 weeks): demonstrate 35–55% unit cost delta via batching + caching + routing; target realistic realized savings of $6–10k/month run-rate for reconciliation path.

Suggested pilot scope (minimal viable pilot)
- Duration: 3 weeks (1 week baseline collect, 2 weeks controlled run).
- Traffic: start with 20% of reconciliation traffic (non-peak windows), then stretch to peak-day test.
- Success criteria: >30% realized per-token cost decrease without >15% negative impact on P95 latency for customer-facing calls.

Attachments: I will send a sizing workbook and a short SOW draft (pilot_sizing.xlsx, redwood_poc_sow_draft.pdf).

Immediate next steps
1) Arielle — confirm procurement timeline & any hard budget ceilings for Q4.
2) KineticPay engineering — share a 48-hour request sample (anonymized) we can use to validate batching cadence.
3) Redwood (Marissa / me) — share pilot sizing + SOW, and set a 30-minute alignment call early next week to pin dates.

Thanks — happy to hop on another sync if you want to run the numbers live.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pilot_sizing.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: redwood_poc_sow_draft.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Arielle Kwon <arielle.k@kineticpay.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-27T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: KineticPay discovery — token economics & pilot affordability

Sean — thanks for the thorough recap. This aligns well with what Tom and I took away. A couple of clarifications and constraints from our side: 

Clarifications / constraints
- Budget: for Q4 we have a hard ceiling of ~$40k incremental for POCs across vendors — we need to keep the ask modest and defensible.
- Procurement window: procurement review starts 2026-09-15 and we need a SOW + cost estimate by 2026-09-08 to make that cycle.
- Data-sharing: engineering can produce a 48-hour anonymized request log by EOD Tuesday (Aug 31). That will contain request/response sizes and timestamps.

What would help from Redwood
- An explicit example ROI: take sample day of 1.2M tokens and show month-over-month $ savings under conservative/median/optimistic scenarios.
- A scoped pilot that fits the $40k-ish cap (including any reserved capacity fees).

We can do the alignment call next Tuesday (Sep 1) at 10am PDT — is that open on your side?

Appreciate it — Arielle
Arielle Kwon
Head of AI Platforms | KineticPay

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Arielle Kwon <arielle.k@kineticpay.com>, Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@kineticpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-28T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: KineticPay discovery — token economics & pilot affordability

Arielle — great, thanks for the constraints. I iterated the pilot to fit under your $40k cap and attached a short workbook with a modeled ROI (conservative/median/optimistic tabs). Summary here: 

Pilot proposal (fit-for-procurement)
- Scope: 3-week pilot, 20% traffic slice (reconciliation backfill + low-latency confirmations), includes Redwood hosted runtime for the pilot window.
- Estimated cost: $28k–$36k total (depends on traffic stretch & optional reserved burst capacity). Workbook shows breakouts.
- Expected realized savings: 32% conservative / 42% median / 56% optimistic on per-inference unit economics for the targeted slice (main drivers: batching 1.7x, caching 18% hit rate, model routing 35% CPU savings).

What we need from KineticPay to start
- Anonymized 48-hour request sample (baseline) — engineering ETA Aug 31.
- Procurement contact for SOW routing — name/email so we can draft the procurement-ready SOW.

Suggested schedule
- Tue 2026-09-01 10:00am PDT — 30 min alignment (we'll review workbook + SOW).
- Week of 2026-09-06 — baseline collection & Redwood run in staging.
- Week of 2026-09-20 — pilot stretch and final readout.

Attachments included: pilot_sizing.xlsx (ROI tabs + assumptions) and redwood_poc_sow_draft.pdf (procurement-ready language we can tailor).

If that works I will: (a) lock the Sep 1 slot on our calendars, (b) drop a short procurement SOW email to your procurement contact once you share the name, (c) spin up the pilot environment once we have the sample.

Best regards,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
